content.text:
I couldn't reproduce this. The tape already shows the same text as the display.

I ran both cases in headless Chrome against the current `index.html`:

| Keys | Display | Tape line | Tape result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.1 + 0.2 = | `0.3` | `0.1 + 0.2` | `0.3` |
| 1 ÷ 3 = | `0.3333333333` | `1 ÷ 3` | `0.3333333333` |

I also tried reusing a result after `=`, using ± on a result, and putting a result inside parentheses. Every visible tape line matched the display.

`0.30000000000000004` only shows up in the hidden `data-value` attribute. The display has the same hidden value, so the two still match. That follows DEC-004: numbers are rounded only when shown, never when stored. The row's text is rounded by `formatNumber` (`index.html:174`). If the user saw the long number, it most likely came from a tool reading that attribute, or from an older copy of the page.

I changed nothing. If they can tell me exactly which keys they pressed and where they saw the long number, I'll look again.
